newsitem.title: USA: Texas Meridian abandons "Deep Saline" well.
newsitem.headline: Texas Meridian abandons "Deep Saline" well.

text.p: Texas Meridian Resources Corp said Monday operations on the LL&E Fee No. 1 "Deep Saline" well have ceased after unsuccessful attempts to recover a stuck formation testing tool.
The company has an 87.5 percent working interest in the well, which is being plugged and abandoned, spokesman W. Matt Ralls said. The remaining eighth is held by individuals.

The company noted it took over operations from Louisiana Land & Exploration Co on December 10 at a depth of 21,780 feet with the objective of deepening the well to penetrate the original target horizon, the Duval sand.
The Duval sand was encountered at 21,810 feet and contained more than 300 feet of gross sand interval.
Initial logging indicated the presence of hydrocarbons in the zone, but calculated porosities were insufficient to support a completion attempt without further information, Texas Meridian said.
When the company attempted to run a Schlumberger Ltd formation testing tool to determine the productive capability of the Duval sand, the tool became stuck and the wireline conveying the tool parted.
After extensive fishing operations, the tool and over two thousand feet of wireline were unable to be retrieved.

Concurrent with fishing operations, the company said, it conducted further detailed analysis of the electric log data that, in the absence of data from the formation testing tool, did not support the conclusion that expected producing rates and reserve volumes would be adequate to justify the expense to complete the well. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
